title: Principles of social justice in health

draft.title: Principles of social justice in health
card: Social justice means everyone has a fair chance to be healthy. Health promotion uses three principles to work towards this: equity, diversity and supportive environments.
fairness, not sameness. People with greater need get more support, so that everyone has a fair chance of good health.
people differ in culture, age, language, ability and where they live. Programs should respect these differences and be designed so that different groups can use them.
settings that make the healthy choice easier, such as safe parks, clean water and welcoming services. Everyone should be able to reach them.
draft.remember: Social justice in health means fair chances for all, which can mean giving more help to those who need it most.

a.q: Which action best shows the principle of equity in health promotion?
opts: Giving more support to groups with greater health needs
Giving every suburb exactly the same amount of funding
Running one program in English for the whole population
Letting each person pay for the services they choose
a.why: Equity means fairness, so people with greater need receive more support. Giving every suburb the same funding sounds fair, but it is equality, and it ignores that some groups start with greater need.

b.q: A council finds that few recent migrants use its free health checks. Staff offer the checks in several languages at community centres the migrants already visit. Which principle does this mainly show?
opts: Diversity, as the program fits different language needs
Equity, as every resident gets an identical service
Supportive environments, as it builds new parks
Social justice, as it removes the need for health checks
b.why: Offering the checks in several languages at familiar places responds to differences in language and culture, which is diversity. Equity is tempting, but an identical service for everyone is not what the council did. It changed the service to suit one group.
b.clue: Look at what the council changed to suit the migrants' differences.

a.best: Giving more support to groups with greater health needs

b.best: Diversity, as the program fits different language needs
